frame: Course ENU: metres; x east, y north, z up; origin at enclosure floor centre

start._note: User-requested launch position 8 inches (0.2032 m) forward of the imported mark, along the unchanged 90-degree heading (+course y). Physically place the drone here before starting the stack. Not a surveyed venue pose.

vehicle._note: 7-inch propeller diameter confirmed by Matthew on 2026-11-07: 7 * 0.0254 = 0.1778 m. Rotor XY positions are the fleet FRD allocator geometry copied from deploy/px4/params/07_airframe_geometry.params (drone 20 FC, 2026-11-01); no runtime sibling-repository dependency. Horizontal yaw-independent reach = max(hypot(x,y)) + diameter/2 = 0.29408284528683193 m. coursenav.airframe derives at load and retains any larger declared envelope. Not a surveyed 3-D tilt/guard envelope.
vehicle._margin_note: Existing 0.12 m planning margin retained, separately from physical reach: planned minimum now 0.4140828452868319 m. This margin originated in 2026-11-05 offline corridor-block experiments, not a measured tracking/estimation bound. Run010 showed about 0.123 m transverse setpoint error, so retaining it is not a contact-free guarantee.

keepout._note: stay off the boulders so the downward rangefinder never steps: VL53L1X 27 deg cone at 0.8 m is ~0.07 m radius at boulder-top height; 0.25 m adds position error. Boulder tops (0.53 m) are below refnav's band (cruise 0.8 - band_m 0.25 = 0.55 m), so refnav does not treat them as obstacles.

sequence.name: tunnel
sequence._note: Checkpoint 3: fly the tube's axis, entering at the end nearer the maze. Expands to tunnel_entry (align: entry_m before the mouth, far enough for the camera to see both rim edges: a 0.63 m half-bore needs 0.9 m plus the camera offset) and tunnel_exit (straight, exit_m past the far end).

sequence.name: tunnel_clearance
sequence._note: Required full stop beyond the tunnel before turning toward the window. Approximate placement from the user's pink waypoint, not surveyed. Existing align approach mode preserves a stopping navigator leg; no gate-alignment geometry is attached. This goal cannot be dropped as a via point or smoothed into the following leg. Map geometry is unchanged.

sequence.name: pad
sequence._note: User-measured final landing goal: 0.75 m farther from the start along the vertical map axis (-course y), then 0.40 m diagonally toward -x/-y (south-west) after a flight landed on the pad's far edge, diagonally right of centre. Applies an offset to the imported pad centre; target (-2.3250, -1.8253) m. OBJ/voxel map and marking radius are unchanged.

window._height_note: User-measured approximate opening: sill 1.0 m, height 0.8 m. Stop at window_pre, climb and settle at 1.4 m before alignment; retain crossing height until landing. Vertical bounds override the old OBJ opening for alignment only; the OBJ/voxel map is unchanged.
window._note: Checkpoint 4 (+5 points): the opening in wall C2a at cruise height, crossed towards the pad. depth_m: the pre point (alignment hover) 0.8 m before the plane, the farthest free point from which the camera (0.116 m ahead, 35 deg usable half-FOV) sees both jambs; post_m: the exit point.

gate_b._note: Checkpoint 4: the gap past wall C2b's end that the drone fits through, crossed towards the pad. The crossing direction is SEARCHED within +-cross_search_deg of the gap's perpendicular for the most clearance whose approach does not face a surface (planner.gate_crossing); nothing is typed in.

return._note: Automatic after confirmed pad landing/disarm, only if fresh telemetry, battery, localization, reset continuity, full-trip time and 3D map-clearance checks pass. Otherwise remain landed. 2.3 m is the operator-selected return height; physical clearance is not certified by this setting. Target is this run's remembered launch pose, checked against the derived mark; no prior-run replay.
return._enabled_note: matthew930am: off for run013 (steady course, Flight PASS 0.305 m grader truth clearance); re-enabled after that pass at Matthew's request. The return itself has still never flown.

navigation._flow_note: FLOW-CORNERS (2026-11-07): path mode as a hybrid. Bends sharper than stop_turn_deg 60 are stop-and-turn (as steady: no yaw while moving through big heading changes); gentler bends are arcs flown without stopping, the heading never leading the tangent by more than refnav path_heading_lead_deg 25 (run010 contact: 50 deg of preview) and turning at most yaw_rate_dps 30 while moving. Speed per point = min(cruise 0.5, tube / tube_response_s 0.44 s with tube = (clearance - reach) / 2: steady run015's cross-track model, as planner.leg_speed_mps; lateral accel 0.3; clearance slow-down); the approach to every stop is capped by the stop-overshoot fit -0.081 + 0.576 v + 0.10 m (runs 015+016, planner.end_room_speed_mps) against the mapped room beyond it. refnav path_tube_gate: outside the local tube -> forward speed capped by path_tube_recovery_mps while the setpoint beside the aircraft corrects cross-track error. cruise 0.5 is above the 0.40 m/s flown in runs 015/016: it is reached only where the tube allows (clearance >= 0.73 m), i.e. open floor, and is unflown.
navigation._note: Path mode: refnav stops at declared stops and follows navigator paths between them. Historical offline figures in older notes used the 0.28 m synthetic aircraft. The confirmed 7-inch profile resolves to radius 0.294082845 m; full-course planning currently refuses at the retained 0.12 m margin. The diagnostic mission has a separate slow transit and bounded measurement schedule; see docs/RUN010_CONTACT_AND_NEXT_DIAGNOSTIC.md.

refnav._tube_recovery_note: Outside the path tube, cap forward speed at 0.10 m/s while position feedback recenters; resume the planned speed inside half the tube. Replaces the previous zero-forward-speed hold. Planned stops, depth and path freshness, obstacle and estimator checks still apply. Not flight validated.

steady._note: STEADY (matthew930am, 2026-11-07): untuned, conservative course profile. Every value is a choice from recorded evidence, not a fit. Straight legs only (planner waypoints, no navigator arcs): runs 006-010 measured PX4 cross-track p95 0.036-0.069 m on straight non-yawing motion at <= 0.16 m/s, but 0.10-0.15 m on curving paths and 0.06-0.26 m while yawing during translation, and ~0.19 m on straight legs above 0.16 m/s (run004). Hence speed 0.15, blend_turn_deg 0 (every vertex: stop, settle below 0.05 m/s for 0.5 s, turn in place, depth-check, go), heading fixed while moving (pose mode updates yaw only when blending). PX4's velocity estimate departs from truth for ~2 s during every ~50 deg yaw-while-moving sweep (runs 004-010; EV velocity is not fused, EKF2_EV_CTRL 9, so not a frame bug): yawing only while stopped avoids it. tube_gate: forward motion holds while the aircraft is more than the leg's tube_m (planner.leg_tube_m = half the leg's physical slack) across the leg. accel/brake 0.5 m/s^2 (was 0.3; 3-minute rule): braking from the 0.30 m/s cap takes 0.09 m, inside capture_m 0.10. Arrival settle 0.3 s below 0.08 m/s (was 0.5 s / 0.05).
steady._settle_note: Set-off drift (first 2.5 s of a leg, across it) median ~0.07 m in run013 (face_tol 8, no settle) and in run015 (face_tol 3 + 2 s settle): neither the tighter heading tolerance nor the settle changed it, so both are back to the flown run013 values (face_tol_deg 8, turn_settle_s 0).
steady._speed_note: RULE 7.9: a run ends at the 3-minute limit (clock from leaving the launch mark, rule 7.5). run015 took ~287 s. Per-leg cruise = planner.leg_speed_mps(tube_m, tube_response_s, leg_speed_cap_mps): tube / 0.44 s, where 0.44 s is run015's measured p90 of (steady cross-track p95 / speed) per leg; cap 0.40 m/s: run016 flew the open legs at 0.25-0.30 m/s with steady cross-track p95/speed 0.11-0.33 s (<= the 0.44 s basis), so the linear relation held there; 0.40 extrapolates it by 1/3. Maze/window legs ~0.15-0.20 m/s, tunnel/chicane ~0.30. speed_mps 0.15 remains the default for legs without a tube. yaw_rate_dps stays at the flown 35: in-place turns slide the body 5-8 cm (runs 013/015, real motion PX4 sees) and vertex clearances are 0.46-0.53 m; a higher rate is unmeasured. hold_s 0.25 (arrival already requires settling).
steady._excite_note: OFF. run017 (b783000) flew excite_yaw 90 at the take-off point: the camera faced the west net at 0.50 m (92 % open, depth sees through it to unmapped space; OAK minimum range 0.4 m) and the estimate failed: the body slid 0.357 m, PX4 local position moved ~1.4 m, xy_valid went false 5.2 s into the yaw and refnav landed (Program FAILED, 7.2 s airborne). From the take-off point every heading except the start one faces a surface at 0.50-0.55 m, which breaks leg_policy face_min_m 0.8 (the rule every in-place turn on the route obeys). A first-yaw excitation needs a place whose whole yaw arc keeps that facing distance; there is none at this start, so it stays off.
steady._first_turn_note: first_turn_gate_s 4.5: after the first >= 20 deg in-place turn only, go once |PX4 - setpoint| < 0.03 m and speed < 0.02 m/s (timeout 4.5 s: run014's 60 deg turn recovered to < 0.03 m at +4.3 s). PX4's post-yaw velocity error: first yaw 0.085 (run015) / 0.091 (run016) m/s, later yaws <= 0.021 / 0.033. Leg 2 (after that turn) was every steady run's minimum leg (0.299, 0.299, 0.277 m) and in run016 spent 6.5 of its 8.1 s creeping on tube holds after a 0.173 m set-off drift.
steady._yaw_profile_note: Before: the turn slewed the yaw setpoint at a constant 35 deg/s from the first tick to the last (yaw acceleration steps) while publishing trajectory_setpoint.yawspeed 0.0 (the message default; run021 published_trajectory), so PX4 followed on feedback alone: ~1.35 s of heading lag per turn (run016). yaw_accel_dps2 90: trapezoidal yaw-rate profile with the rate published as yawspeed feed-forward. 90 deg/s^2 = 35 deg/s over ~one yaw time constant of PX4's default attitude loop (MC_YAW_P 2.8 -> 0.36 s), so the loop can follow the ramp. Whether the abrupt profile drove part of the 5-20 cm in-place slide is the next run's question; the profile is standard multirotor practice either way.
steady._arrival_note: run021 turn diagnosis (bag + truth): the in-place turn started while the aircraft was still arriving, 3.6 cm short and 3.5 cm/s median (13 cm / 7.8 cm/s worst) under the loose test (0.15 m, < 0.08 m/s for 0.3 s); the arrival ran on through the turn and overshot by up to 11 cm: the post-turn reversal. Stops without a turn moved 5-7 cm vs 9-10 cm with one, so yaw adds ~3-4 cm; VIO stayed within 2 cm of truth through every turn. The reversal comes from the tail of that distribution: median handoffs (3.6 cm, 3.5 cm/s) overshot ~1.4 cm, the worst (13 cm / 7.8 cm/s) 8-11 cm. arrive_tight_m 0.05 / arrive_tight_mps 0.03 for arrive_settle_s cuts the tail; 0.03 / 0.02 cost +33 s offline (timeouts) for the median cases; arrive_timeout_s 3.0 after capture falls back to the loose test (PX4's position loop closes with tau ~1.05 s, so ~3 tau reaches the tight bound from the 0.10 m capture). OFF for now (arrive_tight_m 0): in run021/run016 PX4's hold reached 5 cm / 3 cm/s for 0.3 s within 10 s at only 10/20 and 6/20 stops (p50 0.4-0.6 s when it did, p90 1.6-2.5 s), so the gate would often wait for its timeout: +15-30 s per run against the 180 s limit (run021 183.3 s). Enable when the yawspeed feed-forward has bought the time.

navigation._group119_note: group119 = matthew930am (cf48cd8) + flow-corners (32b6d7f). Path mode as flow-corners flew it in run022 (148.2 s sim, Flight PASS 0.281 m), plus matthew930am's: yawspeed feed-forward of the yaw setpoint's rate with a trapezoidal in-place turn (yaw_accel_dps2 90; run021 showed refnav publishing yawspeed 0.0 while slewing, PX4 lagging ~1.4 s), first-turn gate, safe fault landing (refnav_params), and the SIM-ONLY stuck-landing forced disarm (sim_profile).
navigation._arc_tube_note: arc_min_tube_m 0.16: a bend is an arc only where the arc's tube (clearance - reach)/2 is >= 0.16 m everywhere; else stop-and-turn in place. run022 (flow-corners, path mode): PX4 cross-track p95 in 'go' was 0.039-0.099 m without recent yaw but 0.122-0.159 m within 2 s of yawing while moving, at every speed band (0.08-0.6 m/s): the arc's yaw adds error that speed does not scale away. 7 of the 10 leg-1 tube holds followed 30 deg/s arc yaw. Maze tubes are 0.07-0.09 m, so maze bends become stop-and-turns (in-place turns after the first show <= 0.028 m/s velocity error); open floor keeps its arcs.
navigation._group154_note: group154 (from group119 749bca0): yaw feed-forward OFF (yaw_accel_dps2 0): heading overshoot after in-place turns p50 2.0/1.1 deg without it (run021/run022) vs 19.7/19.1 deg with it (run023/run024, max 52.7), with 0.1-0.2 m body swings (run024 first turn: setpoint 74.3 deg, heading to 94.5 then 68). Path lateral feed-forward clamped to lat_accel_mps2 and zero at stop-and-turn corners (run024 contact at M1: 0.54 m/s^2 lateral feed-forward from the corner's heading kink). Zero-width tubes do not gate.
navigation._center_note: center_stops: each stop-and-turn vertex moves to the highest-clearance point of its corner region (within half the shorter adjacent segment), keeping both adjacent segments at the requirement and the depth camera's facing rule (leg_policy face_min_m, or the original vertex's room if less). run029's minimum (0.320 m, M1) was the first in-place turn's ~0.25 m estimator drift at a turn point with 0.516 m clearance where its corner offers 0.566 m.

refnav_params._depth_policy_note: 2026-11-08 user-requested waypoint profile: no observed-path requirement (coverage 0), accept sparse/blank fresh frames (both valid floors 0), no corridor-wait landing (-1), fixed body-origin obstacle threshold 0.35 m (speed scaling off). Missing depth may hide obstacles; camera silence still lands after 5 s. Estimator/PX4, alignment and persistent-obstacle fault handling remains enabled. Supersedes the previous depth settings below.
refnav_params._note: COMPETITION PROFILE: shared by planned routes and offline flight. corridor_half_m remains 0.32 m, which covers the resolved 7-inch horizontal footprint by about 0.026 m; it is not the planner margin. Planner minimum derives from vehicle radius + margin (about 0.4141 m). band_m = plan_band_m; body cruise height is cruise_z_m above floor.
refnav_params._previous_profile_note: Team-approved loosening (2026-11-06 flights A-E, see HANDOFF): hold-and-recheck before landing on 'route blocked' (4 s hover, 0.2 m back-off, 2 s recheck); depth silence not counted in turns/holds, land after 5 s (was 3); 3 confirming frames (was 2); stop distance max(0.55, 0.45 + 1.0 * v) (was 0.9 fixed); corridor coverage 0.45 (was 0.6); valid pixels 0.15 while static (0.3 moving); corridor wait 10 s (was 8). NOT loosened: landing on unhealthy estimator / invalid PX4 position, yielding when PX4 leaves Offboard, never translating into a confirmed obstacle, the height limit, every PX4-side setting. tunnel_align_max_age_s 6 s: the mouth is 1.15 m past the entry point (where both rim edges are in view), ~4.3 s at 0.3 m/s with the ramp and the check; the aircraft does not turn in between.
refnav_params._align_note: Window: fixed 1.40 m floor-referenced target at window_pre, with XY held during the climb. Measured height within 0.05 m continuously for 1 s releases alignment; repeat the hold after camera trim (max +/-0.10 m). Missing/inconsistent edges keep the nominal height. Retain the crossing target through the pad approach. Tunnel correction limit remains 0.15 m. Heading correction remains disabled. User opening bounds override the lower OBJ window for alignment only; the old map does not verify the raised crossing.
refnav_params._correction_note: correction_*: bounded map corrections (coursenav.loc_node -> /coursenav/px4_correction) shift the REMAINING targets at every leg start. Offline (2026-11-06): a 0.40 m total cap and a 0.06 m deadband let the correction lag the drift by 0.1-0.2 m, which was the margin at the M3 corner and the window; VIO can drift 0.3-0.5 m over the 17 m course, so the cap is 0.8 m (the enclosure bounds the localizer anyway), 0.2 m per leg start, 4 cm deadband. correction_rate_mps 0.05: the targets also follow the correction during a leg (at most 5 cm per second of shift), so the aircraft stays on the corrected line between leg starts; offline the leg-start-only rule lagged 0.1 m at the M3 corner and grazed it.
refnav_params._safe_land_note: Fault landings descend only over a floor column clear of published surfaces within rotor reach + margin (coursenav.course.land_columns, full 3-D map floor..band top); otherwise refnav retraces its flown path to the nearest clear column first. run012: a fault land-in-place over the tube came down onto it. Estimator / PX4-position failures still land at once.

_goals_note: Temporary map-based policy. First semantic goal is tunnel; original downstream tunnel/window/pad features are measured from this reconstructed OBJ.

enclosure._note: The net's inner planes, measured on the OBJ's 'Net side' groups at load (coursenav.semantics). The net is 92% open: depth sees THROUGH it to unmapped things. Beyond it is UNKNOWN, not free: the localizer's likelihood field is 0 there and the body may not be there (live diagnosis 2026-11-06).

chicane_scoring._note: Chicane choice (planner.plan_options): score = option points - time_points_per_s * estimated time - clearance_penalty_per_cm per cm the plan's min clearance is below clearance_min_m - facing_penalty per leg end facing a surface closer than leg_policy.face_min_m (or an infeasible crossing) - alignment_penalty per gate whose edges the camera cannot see from its pre point. Scores and the reason are logged at planning time.

leg_policy._note: Leg-end rule (planner.fix_leg_ends): no leg may end where a mapped surface lies within face_min_m along the next heading (the OAK's 0.4 m blind range put flight E's depth at 5 % valid facing the barrier at 0.47 m) or within arc_min_m anywhere in the in-place turn's arc; via points are moved back along their incoming leg up to move_max_m. Legs shorter than min_leg_m and corners under collinear_deg are merged. passage_min_frac: a straight leg with a roof and walls on both sides over this fraction is a passage (tunnel mode). overrun_min_m: no mapped surface within this distance beyond a leg's end along the leg's own heading (refnav's leg_end_margin_m 0.25 + 0.15 slack), else refnav calls the leg blocked. face_relaxed_m: a via point that cannot be moved to give face_min_m (maze corners: the divider end is 0.6-0.8 m ahead of the next leg) may face a surface down to this, which still clears the camera's blind range (0.4 m + the 0.12 m camera offset) by a margin.
leg_policy._keep_path_clearance_note: planner._simplify_idx: shortcuts keep the clearance of the A* sub-path they replace, capped at 0.6 m = the A* prefer_m (beyond it A* itself does not centre), less half a cell. 0 restores greedy shortcuts.

sim_profile._fixture_skybeta_note: kestral_nav934am (skybeta): the drone starts ON the launch mark (rule 7.4; the FlyX training spawn was [0.0, 0.2])
sim_profile._note: SIMULATION / TRAINING ONLY. The prepared-training world spawns the aircraft 20 cm north of the launch mark (environment.json); this declared offset gives the localizer's prior and the offline tools their start. It is not competition configuration: at the venue the start is the mark itself and fly_course.py takes the start pose from the localizer.
sim_profile._refnav_note: DISABLED after run023 (cf48cd8): the forced disarm fired with the aircraft 0.75 m in the air. After a Boulder 5 strike on leg 20 knocked it ~0.9 m sideways, the rangefinder read 0.079 m over raised geometry (not the floor), PX4's estimate had jumped (VIO re-anchor, height -7.66 m), so both 'touchdown' and 'divergence' tests passed in the air; it fell and came to rest at 106 deg tilt. A short rangefinder reading is not evidence of touchdown wherever anything is mapped below the flight path. Kept off until a touchdown test independent of the rangefinder's surface exists. Original problem (run019: PX4 never confirming a real touchdown) remains open for the organizers.
